name: Kisan Credit Card
description: Provides farmers with timely, low-interest credit for cultivation and related needs through a single card.
benefits: Short-term credit for crops, farm inputs and allied activities
Interest subvention on timely repayment
Collateral-free loans up to a prescribed limit
Covers farming, animal husbandry and fisheries

other_conditions: Owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, sharecroppers and self-help groups can apply
Applicants above 60 may need a co-borrower

eligibility_text: You should be a farmer, tenant farmer, sharecropper or part of a farmers' group
You should be between 18 and 75 years old
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest bank branch (commercial, regional rural or cooperative bank)
Ask for the Kisan Credit Card application form and fill it in
Submit it with land and identity documents
The bank verifies your details and issues the card
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round, and the card is renewed periodically.

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
description: Crop insurance that protects farmers against yield loss from natural calamities, pests and diseases.
benefits: Insurance cover for notified crops against non-preventable natural risks
Low fixed premium for farmers, with the rest subsidised
Claims for losses from drought, flood, pests and unseasonal rain

other_conditions: Crop must be notified for your area in that season
Tenant farmers and sharecroppers can enrol with proper documents
Enrolment must be done before the cut-off date for the season

eligibility_text: You should be a farmer growing a notified crop in a notified area
Tenant farmers and sharecroppers are also eligible
how_to_apply: Apply through your bank, a Common Service Centre (CSC), an insurance company agent, or the PMFBY portal
Declare the crop and area you have sown
Pay your share of the premium
Keep the receipt and policy number for claims
deadline_info: Cut-off dates differ by state and season (kharif and rabi). Check the current dates on the portal.

name: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
ministry: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (National Health Authority)
description: Health insurance that covers hospitalisation costs for eligible families at government and empanelled private hospitals, without payment at the point of care.
benefits: Health cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year
Cashless treatment for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation
Covers pre- and post-hospitalisation expenses, diagnostics and medicines
No cap on family size or age of members
Senior citizens aged 70 and above are covered regardless of income

other_conditions: Eligibility is based on the deprivation and occupational criteria of the SECC 2011 database, not on a simple income limit
Rural families: those in deprivation categories such as kuccha housing, no adult earning member, landless manual labour, or SC/ST households
Urban families: listed occupations such as rag pickers, domestic workers, street vendors, construction workers, sanitation workers
Citizens aged 70 and above are eligible irrespective of income
Some states run their own expanded versions, so check your state's rules

eligibility_text: Eligibility depends on your family's inclusion in the official SECC 2011 list, not just your income
Senior citizens aged 70 and above can enrol regardless of income
You can check your name on the official portal or at a Common Service Centre
exclusions: Families not covered by the SECC deprivation or occupational criteria (unless the state extends coverage)
documents: Ration card or other family ID
how_to_apply: Check whether you are eligible on the official PM-JAY portal using your mobile number or ration card
Visit a Common Service Centre or an empanelled hospital's Ayushman Mitra desk
Complete e-KYC (usually with Aadhaar) to get your Ayushman card
Show the card at an empanelled hospital for cashless treatment
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. You can enrol at any time if you are eligible.

name: Janani Suraksha Yojana
ministry: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (National Health Mission)
description: A cash incentive for pregnant women who deliver in a government or accredited private health facility, meant to reduce maternal and newborn deaths.
benefits: Cash assistance after delivery in a government or accredited health facility
Amount depends on whether you live in a rural or urban area and on your state's category
Support from an ASHA worker for registration, transport and facility delivery

other_conditions: Applicant must be a pregnant woman who delivers in a government or accredited private facility
In Low Performing States, all pregnant women are eligible regardless of age or number of births
In High Performing States, only BPL, SC and ST women aged 19 and above are eligible, for up to two live births

eligibility_text: You should be a pregnant woman planning to deliver in a government or accredited facility
Extra conditions (age, BPL/SC/ST status, number of births) apply in some states
Your ASHA worker can tell you which rules apply in your state
exclusions: Home deliveries (except in certain cases specified under the scheme)
documents: JSY or Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card
BPL card or SC/ST certificate (where required in your state)
Proof of registration for antenatal care
how_to_apply: Register the pregnancy at your nearest Anganwadi, sub-centre or health facility
Contact your ASHA worker, who will guide you and help with documents
Deliver at a government or accredited private facility
The incentive is paid to your bank account or by cheque after delivery
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. Register during pregnancy, and the incentive is paid after delivery.

name: Begum Hazrat Mahal National Scholarship
ministry: Ministry of Minority Affairs (Maulana Azad Education Foundation)
description: A scholarship for meritorious girl students from notified minority communities studying in classes 9 to 12, to help them continue their schooling.
benefits: Annual scholarship amount for class 9 and 10 students of Rs 5,000
Higher annual amount for class 11 and 12 students of Rs 6,000
Renewal in the following year if the student continues to meet the conditions

other_conditions: Must belong to a notified minority community (Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain or Parsi)
Must be studying in class 9 to 12
Must have scored at least 50% marks in the previous class
Family annual income should not exceed Rs 2 lakh
Check on the portal whether the scheme is open for the current academic year

eligibility_text: You should be a girl student in class 9 to 12
You should belong to a notified minority community
You should have at least 50% marks in your previous class
Your family's annual income should be within the limit set by the scheme
exclusions: Students who are already getting another scholarship of the same kind
documents: Income certificate of parents or guardian
Bank account details of the student
School or institution ID or bonafide certificate
how_to_apply: Register on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) with your details
Select the Begum Hazrat Mahal National Scholarship and fill in the application
Upload the required documents
Submit, then have the application verified by your school
deadline_info: Applications open once a year, and the last date changes every academic year. Check the National Scholarship Portal for the current dates.

name: PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students
ministry: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education)
description: A merit-based scholarship for students who score in the top percentile in class 12 and go on to regular college or university courses.
benefits: Annual scholarship for the first three years of a degree of Rs 12,000 per year
Higher annual amount for the final years of longer courses and for postgraduate study of Rs 20,000 per year
Renewed each year if the student keeps up attendance and passes the year

other_conditions: Must have scored above the 80th percentile in the class 12 board exam in your stream
Must be studying a regular degree course at a recognised college or university
Distance, correspondence and private-mode courses are not covered
Family annual income should not exceed Rs 4.5 lakh
Renewal needs a minimum attendance and passing the year

eligibility_text: You should have scored in the top 20 percent of your class 12 board in your stream
You should be doing a regular degree course at a recognised institution
Your family's annual income should be within the limit set by the scheme
exclusions: Students on distance or correspondence courses
Students already getting another central scholarship for the same course
documents: College admission proof or bonafide certificate
Bank account details of the student
how_to_apply: Register on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP)
Select the Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship and fill in the application
Upload the required documents
Submit, then have the application verified by your institution
deadline_info: Applications open once a year, and the last date changes every academic year. Check the National Scholarship Portal for the current dates.

name: PM Vidyalaxmi
ministry: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education)
description: Collateral-free and guarantor-free education loans for students admitted to top-ranked higher education institutions, with interest support for lower-income families.
benefits: Education loan without collateral or a third-party guarantor
Government credit guarantee on part of the loan of 75% for loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh
Interest subvention for students from lower-income families
Single online application for loans and interest support

other_conditions: Must be admitted to a notified quality higher education institution
Interest subvention applies only to families under a set income limit of Rs 8 lakh, with fuller support at around Rs 4.5 lakh
Students eligible for other government scholarships or interest subsidies may not get interest subvention under this scheme
The final loan is sanctioned by the bank as per its own rules

eligibility_text: You should have secured admission in a notified top higher education institution
The loan itself does not depend on family income, but interest support does
The final approval is given by the bank
exclusions: Students admitted to institutions that are not on the notified list
how_to_apply: Register on the PM Vidyalaxmi portal
Fill in the common education loan application
Choose the banks you want to apply to and upload the documents
Track the application and sanction status on the portal
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. Apply after you receive an admission offer, and in time for fee payment.

name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme)
description: A monthly pension for elderly people from below poverty line households.
benefits: Monthly pension from the Centre for those aged 60 to 79 of Rs 200
Higher monthly central pension for those aged 80 and above of Rs 500
Many states add their own top-up, so the final amount varies by state

other_conditions: Applicant must belong to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) household as per state or Centre lists
Age 60 and above for the pension, and 80 and above for the higher central amount
States may set their own income or age rules, so check your state's criteria

eligibility_text: You should be 60 years or older
Your household should be below the poverty line
State rules can differ, so check with your local office
exclusions: Households that are not on the BPL list (unless the state extends coverage)
documents: Age proof (Aadhaar, birth certificate or school certificate)
Bank account or post office account details
how_to_apply: Contact your Gram Panchayat, Block office, Municipality or the district social welfare office
Fill in the pension application form and attach documents
The local authority verifies your age and BPL status
Once approved, the pension is paid monthly to your bank or post office account
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. You can apply at any time once you meet the age and BPL conditions.

name: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme)
description: A monthly pension for widows from below poverty line households.
benefits: Monthly central pension for eligible widows of Rs 300
Higher central amount from age 80 of Rs 500
Many states add their own top-up, so the final amount varies by state

other_conditions: Applicant must be a widow
Applicant must belong to a BPL household
Age 40 to 79 for the standard pension, and women aged 80 and above are covered under the old-age scheme's higher amount
States may set their own rules, so check your state's criteria

eligibility_text: You should be a widow aged between 40 and 79
Your household should be below the poverty line
State rules can differ, so check with your local office
exclusions: Widows from households that are not on the BPL list (unless the state extends coverage)
documents: Age proof (Aadhaar, birth certificate or school certificate)
Bank account or post office account details
how_to_apply: Contact your Gram Panchayat, Block office, Municipality or the district social welfare office
Fill in the widow pension application form and attach the death certificate and other documents
The local authority verifies your details and BPL status
Once approved, the pension is paid monthly to your bank or post office account
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. You can apply at any time once you meet the conditions.

name: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme)
description: A monthly pension for persons with severe or multiple disabilities from below poverty line households.
benefits: Monthly central pension for eligible persons with disabilities of Rs 300
Higher central amount from age 80 of Rs 500
Many states add their own top-up, so the final amount varies by state

other_conditions: Applicant must have a severe or multiple disability of 80%
Applicant must belong to a BPL household
Age 18 to 79 for the standard pension
A disability certificate or UDID card from a competent medical authority is needed

eligibility_text: You should be aged between 18 and 79
You should have a severe or multiple disability, certified by a medical authority
Your household should be below the poverty line
exclusions: Persons whose disability is below the required threshold
Households that are not on the BPL list (unless the state extends coverage)
documents: Age proof (Aadhaar, birth certificate or school certificate)
Bank account or post office account details
how_to_apply: Contact your Gram Panchayat, Block office, Municipality or the district social welfare office
Fill in the disability pension application form and attach the disability certificate and other documents
The local authority verifies your disability and BPL status
Once approved, the pension is paid monthly to your bank or post office account
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. You can apply at any time once you meet the conditions.

name: Atal Pension Yojana
description: A voluntary, contribution-based pension scheme that gives a guaranteed monthly pension after age 60, mainly for workers in the unorganised sector.
benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension from age 60 of Rs 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000, depending on your contribution
Pension continues for your spouse after your death, and then the corpus goes to your nominee
Government co-contribution for some subscribers who joined earlier

other_conditions: Must have a savings bank account or post office savings account
Must have a mobile number linked to the account
Income tax payers are not eligible to join
Contribution amount depends on your joining age and chosen pension amount

eligibility_text: You should be between 18 and 40 years old
You should have a bank or post office savings account
Income tax payers cannot join under the current rules
exclusions: Income tax payers
People already getting benefits under a statutory social security scheme
documents: Savings bank account or post office account details
how_to_apply: Visit the bank or post office where you hold your savings account
Fill in the APY registration form and choose your pension amount
Give consent for monthly auto-debit from your account
Keep the acknowledgement or PRAN details for future reference
deadline_info: No fixed deadline, but you must join before turning 40. Later joining means higher contributions.

name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
description: Support for urban families without a pucca house to buy, build or improve a home, mainly through a subsidy on home loan interest.
benefits: Interest subsidy on home loans for eligible urban families
Subsidy amount and loan limit depend on your income group
Support for building or enhancing a house on your own land
Houses are meant to be registered in the name of a woman or jointly

other_conditions: Family must not own a pucca house anywhere in India
Family must not have taken benefit under any earlier central housing scheme
Applies to urban areas only, as notified under the scheme
Income groups are EWS, LIG and MIG, with different limits and benefits
Family includes husband, wife and unmarried children

eligibility_text: You should live in an urban area covered by the scheme
Your family should not own a pucca house anywhere in India
Your household income should fall within the EWS, LIG or MIG limits
You should not have taken benefit under an earlier central housing scheme
exclusions: Families that already own a pucca house
Families that already received benefit under another central housing scheme
documents: Aadhaar card of all adult family members
Property documents, if building or enhancing on your own land
Self-declaration of not owning a pucca house
how_to_apply: Check the official PMAY-Urban portal for the current application route
Apply online, or through your bank, housing finance company or Urban Local Body office
Fill in your family, income and property details
Upload documents and submit, then track the application with the reference number
deadline_info: The scheme runs for a limited period set by the government. Check the official portal for the current end date.

name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin
description: Financial help for rural families who are homeless or live in kuccha or dilapidated houses to build a pucca house with basic amenities.
benefits: Financial assistance to build a pucca house of Rs 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly and difficult areas
Additional support for toilet construction under Swachh Bharat Mission
Up to 90 to 95 days of unskilled wage employment under MGNREGA for construction
Option of a loan of up to Rs 70,000

other_conditions: Applies to rural areas only
Family must be homeless or live in a kuccha or dilapidated house with one or two rooms
Beneficiaries are selected from the SECC 2011 data and verified by the Gram Sabha
Priority goes to SC/ST families, freed bonded labourers, minorities and persons with disabilities
Family should not own a motorised vehicle, mechanised farm equipment or a Kisan Credit Card with a credit limit above a set amount

eligibility_text: You should live in a rural area
Your family should be homeless or live in a kuccha or badly damaged house
Your name should be on the official beneficiary list, which is based on SECC 2011 and verified by the Gram Sabha
exclusions: Families that already own a pucca house
Families that meet the exclusion criteria, such as owning a motorised vehicle or having a high income
documents: Land ownership or allotment proof, if applicable
how_to_apply: Check whether your family is on the PMAY-G beneficiary list, using the official portal or by asking your Gram Panchayat
If you are missing and believe you qualify, contact your Gram Panchayat or Block Development Office
Complete verification and geo-tagging of the existing house site
Once sanctioned, receive funds in your bank account in instalments linked to construction progress
deadline_info: The scheme runs for a limited period set by the government. Check the official portal for the current end date.

name: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana
description: A cash benefit for pregnant and lactating women, meant to partly make up for wage loss and support better nutrition and rest around childbirth.
benefits: Cash benefit of Rs 5,000 in two instalments for the first living child
Rs 6,000 in one instalment for a second child if it is a girl
Money is paid directly into your bank or post office account
Can be received in addition to the JSY cash incentive

other_conditions: Applicant must be a pregnant or lactating woman
Benefit applies to the first living child, and to a second child only if it is a girl
Women who get similar maternity benefits as regular employees of the Centre, a state or a PSU, or under any law, are not eligible
Pregnancy must be registered, and antenatal check-ups and child vaccinations must be completed as required

eligibility_text: You should be a pregnant or lactating woman aged 19 or above
The benefit is for your first living child, and for a second child only if it is a girl
You should not already be getting paid maternity leave benefits from a government job or under another law
exclusions: Women employed in central or state government or PSUs who get maternity benefits
Women getting similar benefits under any other law
documents: Bank or post office account details linked to Aadhaar
Child's birth certificate and vaccination record
how_to_apply: Register the pregnancy at your nearest Anganwadi Centre or approved health facility
Fill in the PMMVY application form and submit it with the documents
Claim each instalment after completing the required check-ups and registrations
Benefit is credited directly to your bank or post office account
deadline_info: Apply within the time limits set for each instalment, counted from pregnancy registration and childbirth. Check the portal for the exact limits.

name: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram
ministry: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (National Health Mission)
description: Free healthcare services, with no cash involved, for pregnant women and sick newborns at government health facilities, so that cost does not stop families from seeking care.
benefits: Free normal delivery and caesarean section
Free drugs, consumables, diagnostics and blood
Free diet during your stay (up to 3 days for normal delivery and 7 days for caesarean)
Free transport from home to the facility, between facilities if referred, and back home
Same free services for sick newborns up to one year of age

other_conditions: Applicant must be a pregnant woman using a government health facility
Sick newborns of mothers using these services are also covered
Services are given at government facilities, not private hospitals
No income or BPL condition applies

eligibility_text: You should be a pregnant woman delivering at a government health facility
Your sick newborn is also covered for free care
There is no income condition, and no cash payment is involved
exclusions: Services at private facilities
documents: Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card, if available
how_to_apply: No separate application is needed
Register the pregnancy at your nearest Anganwadi, sub-centre or health facility
Contact your ASHA worker, who can arrange free transport
Go to a government facility for delivery, and the free services are given there
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. Services are available throughout pregnancy, delivery and the newborn period.

name: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana
description: Collateral-free loans for small and micro businesses outside agriculture, given through banks, microfinance institutions and NBFCs.
benefits: Shishu loans up to Rs 50,000 for new or very small businesses
Kishor loans from Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh for growing businesses
Tarun loans from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for established businesses
Higher limit for Tarun borrowers who have repaid earlier loans (Tarun Plus up to Rs 20 lakh)
No collateral needed, and no processing fee for Shishu loans

other_conditions: Applicant must run or plan a non-farm, income-generating business in manufacturing, trading or services
Covers small shops, workshops, food businesses, vehicles for commercial use, and similar activities
Direct crop cultivation is not covered, but some allied activities may be
Applicant must not be a loan defaulter, and the bank decides on approval
Loan size depends on your business needs and repayment capacity

eligibility_text: You should be an Indian citizen aged 18 or above with a small business or a plan for one
The business should be outside farming, such as a shop, workshop, service or small manufacturing unit
The final approval is given by the bank or lender
exclusions: Pure agricultural activities such as growing crops
Applicants with defaults on earlier loans
documents: Business proof or business plan (for new businesses, a simple plan or quotations)
how_to_apply: Decide which category (Shishu, Kishor or Tarun) fits your loan amount
Visit a bank branch, microfinance institution or NBFC, or apply through the Udyamimitra portal
Submit the application with identity, address and business documents
The lender assesses your application and releases the loan if approved
deadline_info: No fixed deadline. Loans are available year-round.

name: Stand-Up India
ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services)
description: Bank loans between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs setting up a new business for the first time.
benefits: Composite loan of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore for a new enterprise
Covers both term loan and working capital
Repayment period of up to 7 years, with a moratorium of up to 18 months
Handholding support through the Stand-Up India portal

other_conditions: Applicant must be an SC or ST entrepreneur, or a woman entrepreneur (the two groups are alternatives, so a woman from any category can apply)
The enterprise must be a first-time, greenfield venture in manufacturing, services, trading, or an agri-allied activity
For non-individual businesses, at least 51% of the shareholding and control must be held by an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur
Applicant must not be a defaulter to any bank or financial institution
Borrower is expected to contribute a share of the project cost of 10 percent

eligibility_text: You should be an SC or ST entrepreneur, or a woman entrepreneur, aged 18 or above
The loan is for setting up a brand-new business, not expanding an existing one
The final approval is given by the bank
exclusions: Existing businesses (the loan is only for first-time ventures)
Defaulters to any bank or financial institution
documents: Identity and address proof (Aadhaar, voter ID, etc.)
Proof of business address or premises
how_to_apply: Register on the Stand-Up India portal
Apply through the portal, directly at a bank branch, or through the Lead District Manager
Submit your business plan and documents
The bank evaluates the proposal and sanctions the loan if approved
deadline_info: The scheme was extended for a fixed period, so check the official portal for the current end date.
